name: X-linked erythropoietic protoporphyria

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for X-linked erythropoietic protoporphyria

criteria.description: Early-onset photosensitivity with painful burning and erythema on sun-exposed skin
Markedly elevated erythrocyte protoporphyrin levels with predominance of metal-free protoporphyrin
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the ALAS2 gene on the X chromosome
Evidence of hepatic involvement such as elevated liver enzymes or cholestasis
Histopathological findings consistent with protoporphyria (e.g., subepidermal blistering, thickened dermal collagen)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset photosensitivity, elevated erythrocyte protoporphyrin with metal-free predominance, and pathogenic ALAS2 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Liver involvement may develop later and requires monitoring.

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte protoporphyrin with predominance of metal-free protoporphyrin
Elevated liver function tests (ALT, AST, ALP, bilirubin) in hepatic involvement
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing hepatomegaly or liver fibrosis in advanced disease
other: Skin biopsy showing subepidermal blistering and thickened dermal collagen
Fluorescence spectroscopy of erythrocytes showing protoporphyrin accumulation

distinguishingFeatures: Predominance of zinc protoporphyrin rather than metal-free protoporphyrin
Blistering lesions predominantly on dorsal hands

redFlags: Severe photosensitivity with blistering and scarring
Signs of hemolytic anemia or hepatic encephalopathy
